Overview: The desktop distinguishes application input from window-manager commands. Focus determines which application receives ordinary keys.
Setup / example: Open the application menu with the configured WM escape followed by comma. The default WM escape is Ctrl+]. Choose an application; merely reading Help never opens it.
Controls: F6 / Shift-F6 selects the next / previous window. In WM mode, m starts moving and r starts resizing; arrows or hjkl adjust, Enter commits and Esc cancels. X closes and Z maximizes/restores in WM mode.
Tab inside an application changes its pane or control; it does not mean next desktop window. Use the configured WM escape to return to app input.
Settings / defaults / storage: WM escape, move drawing and resize drawing are desktop settings. Outline and live modes are distinct. Layout is saved by the desktop session when that launch permits saving.
Lifecycle: Closing an app window is not the same operation as quitting the desktop. Preserve your session before selecting another installed app release.
Troubleshooting: If keys move windows instead of entering text, check whether WM mode is active. If physical dragging is delayed, a documented binding does not establish that the installed input path is responsive.

Overview: A desktop window can contain several app-owned panes. The focused pane determines list navigation and scrolling.
Setup / example: Open Help from the desktop. Contextual Help is built from the focused app when that app supplies help_pages or registration help. Unavailable app help falls back to Desktop.
Controls: In the existing Help browser, Up/Down or j/k selects entries, Enter opens, Tab changes pane and Esc backs out. / searches the current list. PageUp/PageDown and Home/End scroll reading.

Ctrl-F searches the manual titles, keywords and text. Legacy app-help pages remain available through their app/topic lists and / list search. Open a result with Enter; numbered See also references follow local topics. Backspace returns from a linked topic.
Settings / defaults / storage: Help remembers pane ratio/focus through its existing session adapter. Reading documentation does not change an application setting.
Lifecycle: Opening or searching this manual does not instantiate domain apps, connect services or start radio work. Search indexes the authored manual pages; it does not index every legacy app-help page. See also references open local documentation only.
Troubleshooting: A list search can miss a word that appears only in topic text. Use Ctrl-F for manual text. If a key belongs to a search field, Esc cancels that search before changing focus.

pages.title: Laptop, replay and Nokia launch paths

Overview: The laptop launcher, physical Nokia console helper and development source are separate execution paths. A successful laptop preview is not a Nokia installation.
Setup / example: From the consolidated pocket tree, make n810 launches the local desktop shell. Local services attach after its first display; remote services are selected in Connections. This command does not install a release on the tablet.

On a tablet with the fixed helpers installed, n810-versions selects from the installed app catalog outside the desktop. Close Pocket before switching. The normal tablet launcher is sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/n810-pocket-console run.
Controls: The tablet chooser uses Up/Down or j/k, Enter to select, R to run and Q to quit. Its installed catalog is authoritative.
Settings / defaults / storage: make n810 runs the current consolidated source. The physical tablet runs its selected installed release. Its version can differ until a checked package is installed. Use --no-local-services to start with local services detached.
Lifecycle: A saved configuration snapshot is separate from an app artifact. Restoring an old snapshot must be deliberate with the desktop closed; do not overwrite a running session.
Troubleshooting: If a preview differs from the default, check the selected release and launch path before comparing behavior. Read a current run receipt instead of guessing the newest file is active.
